chapter: Philadelphia, Detroit and back to Atlantic City
title: Frankie Half-Pint Jackson's Palm Sunday joke
summary: Wooding retells how Frankie Jackson preached a risque comic sermon on Jesus, which shocked him.

story.theme_name: Band pranks, jokes and gigs gone wrong
story.community_name: Pranks, practical jokes and band humor

blocks.x: Now, before we leave Atlantic City, I wanted to ask you about some of the other performers who were around when you got back there. Was like, Frankie, 'half-pint', Jackson, was --

Well, Frankie, half-pint, Jackson, Frankie Jackson, I knew him before I left for Newark. Now, he worked up there and there was something I wanted to tell you about him. He said something that was almost a sacrilege. You know how you --he used to talk on the floor between his songs. They all took that from Madison Reed. Madison was the first man used to make up stories on his songs. So he was singing a song, and this was near around Easter time, so he was tellin' the -- preaching. Like a lot of the comedians do in those days. He was preaching this song, and he was preaching about Jesus Christ, see. And he was saying that about Palm Sunday, he said he came into with the crowd all hollering 'Hosanna' and waving palms and all like that. But, he said, 'But these people were sneaky.' He said, 'He come in there on Palm Sunday, and by Wednesday, they put him out.' See, Christ was riding on one of those jackasses. But Frankie didn't say that. He said, 'They put him out, they put his ass out.' See? And I thought this was terrible.

For a man to talk about Jesus Christ like that. And he kept saying it. And a lot of people said, 'Oh!' But it wasn't sacrilege on his part, we thought it. But what he was saying -- they did put him out, and they put his little jackass out. But he didn't say, 'jackass'. He said, 'They put him out and they put his ass out.'
